questions.prompt: What does the Claude Code champion kit say about how adoption of a developer tool usually happens?

options.text: It rarely follows an announcement; it follows people using the tool well in the open.
options.explanation: Right. Someone on the team uses it well, talks about it and makes it easy for others to follow.

options.text: It follows from a rollout announcement, when a senior leader sends it out to everyone in the company.
It happens by itself once every person has an account.
options.explanation: The kit says someone must show how the tool works in the team's real work.

questions.prompt: OpenAI's Usage Insights page: a category has few active users. What does it advise?

options.text: Ask those users how they use it and where they struggle.
options.explanation: Right. They may have a workflow worth sharing or need more support.

options.text: Remove the category from the report, because it is too small.
options.explanation: The page says to ask the people, not to hide the category.

options.text: Scale up the numbers, to estimate the use across the company.
options.explanation: The page warns against scaling up sampled counts.

questions.prompt: What does Anthropic's analytics page say a dip in daily active users may show?

options.text: That the tool is no longer needed anywhere in the company.
options.explanation: The page does not say this.

options.text: That people have found a faster tool somewhere else.
options.explanation: The page does not say this either.

options.text: Friction or issues that need a look.
options.explanation: Right. The page lists dips in usage as a sign of friction or issues.
